aspects.says: A synchronizing wrapper such as Collections.synchronizedMap protects only calls that go through it; a reference to the inner map that outlives the wrap is a path around the lock.
basis: section:A Synchronizing Decorator Protects Only the Calls That Go Through It

aspects.says: Callers that use only a wrapper's methods keep working, unchanged and uncompiled, when the map it keeps privately changes from HashMap to ConcurrentHashMap, and the shared-map races end.
basis: section:Callers That Know Only the Wrapper Run Unchanged When Its HashMap Becomes a ConcurrentHashMap

aspects.says: Map implementations differ on null, so a wrapper keeps its callers independent of the map only if it decides about null itself, failing the same way over every backing.
basis: section:The Swap Is Free Only for What the Wrapper Promises: HashMap Accepted null, ConcurrentHashMap Throws

aspects.says: A decorator's own fields are shared by every thread that uses it and aren't covered by the thread-safety of what it wraps; long counters lose updates, LongAdder doesn't.
basis: section:One Metrics Decorator Serves Every Implementation, and Its Own Counters Must Be Thread-Safe

aspects.says: A decorator implements the interface it wraps and passes each call on, so one class adds metrics to every implementation while callers see the same answers and exceptions.
basis: section:One Metrics Decorator Serves Every Implementation, and Its Own Counters Must Be Thread-Safe

aspects.says: With a metrics decorator and a synchronizing one stacked, the order decides whether the metrics include time spent waiting for the lock.
basis: section:Which Layer Holds the Lock Decides What the Metrics Measure

aspects.says: A subclass of HashMap makes HashMap part of every caller's compiled type, so changing its superclass breaks a caller at run time (IllegalAccessError) and at compile time.
basis: section:Callers That Know Only the Wrapper Run Unchanged When Its HashMap Becomes a ConcurrentHashMap

aspects.says: A decorator that runs every call, reads included, under one lock makes any implementation safe to share.
basis: section:A Synchronizing Decorator Protects Only the Calls That Go Through It

aspects.says: Walking a Collections.synchronizedMap is many calls and must hold the wrapper's lock.
basis: section:A Synchronizing Decorator Protects Only the Calls That Go Through It
aspects.reason: unit 6.5.2 teaches and practises walking a synchronized wrapper; this page names it in one clause

aspects.says: A wrapper that returns its live map or a view hands callers the backing's own iterator behaviour; returning a copy keeps it the same over every backing.
basis: section:The Swap Is Free Only for What the Wrapper Promises: HashMap Accepted null, ConcurrentHashMap Throws
